note: Generated by tools/build-nhl92-patch-analysis.js from the bundled sound slice; do not edit by hand. The decisions about what each patch sounds like are in nhl92-gm-map.json.

method.decode: Z80 register order $30,$38,$34,$3C,... (Z80 $00C5): within a group the operators are op1, op2, op3, op4.
method.music: Each channel's order list walked once (repeats expanded, stopping at the first restart or song switch); pitch is MIDI = note index + 12 after the patch note offset and transpose; frames = duration units x song tempo.
method.sfx: FM SFX streams that load the patch with $80 id; SFX IDs as the game passes them.
method.probe: One note held 40 frames (667 ms) then released, at the patch's median song pitch (C4 if no song uses it), rendered by the step 4 pipeline. Envelope from 5 ms RMS windows; spectrum from a 4096-point FFT 30 ms after onset; flatness over 40 Hz-16 kHz (0 = tonal, 1 = noise); periodicity = best normalised autocorrelation 25 Hz-4 kHz.
